title: 58F type 2 diabetes, poor control, hidden non-adherence

persona.personality: Polite and eager to be seen as a good patient. Deflects when she feels judged.
persona.speech_style: Plain, short answers. Says 'my sugar' for glucose.
concerns: Ending up on dialysis like her mother

chief_complaint: I'm thirsty all the time and I'm up all night going to the bathroom.

clinical_facts.label: Thirst and urination
clinical_facts.value: Increased thirst and nocturia for 3 months

clinical_facts.label: Metformin
clinical_facts.value: 500 mg PO BID, prescribed 14 months ago

clinical_facts.label: Metformin refill history
clinical_facts.value: Pharmacy record shows 2 fills in the last 6 months

clinical_facts.label: Reason for skipped doses
clinical_facts.value: Skips most doses because of diarrhoea and the cost of refills
clinical_facts.patient_phrasing: It tears up my stomach, and it's forty dollars I don't always have.

clinical_facts.label: Sweet tea
clinical_facts.value: Drinks 4 to 5 large glasses of sweet tea a day

trigger_topics: typical day of eating and drinking

clinical_facts.label: Mother's diabetes
clinical_facts.value: Mother had type 2 diabetes and was on dialysis before she died

discrepancies.patient_claim: I take my metformin every day.
discrepancies.truth: She skips most doses because of GI side effects and cost.
discrepancies.reveal_condition: Asked non-judgmentally about side effects or cost, or shown the refill history.

learning_objectives.description: Take a focused history covering symptoms, diet, and family history.
Recognise that reported adherence does not fit the chart, and find out why.
Notice and respond to the patient's fear about where her diabetes is heading.
